Procedures for route planning on the job
Trainers ask staff to read this twice, and by the end of this page you will know why

This page concerns route planning for the Companion Animal Travel Desk of Aurelia Skyways, and it matters because a careful plan protects animal welfare, keeps handoffs orderly, and prevents avoidable stress for travelers and staff alike. When you prepare a booking, begin with the animal's needs, then check the route for any change in handling, climate exposure, or required transfers. If a pet is small, shy, or medically delicate, route choices must favor calm movement and reduced waiting wherever possible.

You must also confirm that the paperwork fits the itinerary. <<FACT F067>> A crate that does not suit the journey can delay acceptance, so review the animal's size, the carrier condition, and any special loading note before you confirm space. For birds, the health documents must be reviewed with equal care. <<FACT F083>> If a certificate is close to expiry, the booking should be paused until the traveler has the correct papers, because a late correction may leave the pet unable to travel.

When speaking with travelers, use plain language and avoid promises that are not yet verified. Explain that the welcome team prepares passengers for boarding, but only after the route, documents, and handling notes are aligned. If a traveler mentions a pet such as Ollie, treat the record as a living case file, not a routine entry. The same method applies whether the traveler is Isaac Tanaka, Gabriel Alvarez, or any other customer: verify, record, and then confirm.

Please remember that route planning is not merely clerical work. It is the point where good judgment protects the animal, supports the traveler, and reduces the chance of an unhappy reroute. What to remember is simple: check the route, check the papers, and never confirm before both are sound.
